title: A shared first step for STX1A families and VAMP2.org / Raging Raymond Foundation

sentences.text: We hope to connect our STX1A families with your VAMP2 community around shared biology: published work links both disorders to reduced protein function.
Intellectual disability and autistic features are reported in both communities.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: The MRC-funded UCL–Yale VAMP2 / SNAREopathy research project and Simons Searchlight offer starting points for discussing shared research approaches.
RARE-X and CMDIR also include SNAP25-related disorders; extending resources to STX1A remains a possibility to check, not a confirmed offer.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: Confirm platform acceptance and adaptations: VAMP2 resources list excessive protein activity, unstable or misfolded proteins, and two unspecified mechanisms not shown for STX1A.
SNAP25 resources list altered proteins blocking working proteins, excessive activity and another unspecified mechanism; autistic behavior is not recorded there.
Check eligibility directly: Searchlight’s SNAP25/VAMP2 coverage comes from its website, not the ClinicalTrials.gov condition list; both epilepsy-dyskinesia studies list STXBP1 and VAMP2.
The congenital myasthenic syndrome trial includes SYT2 and SNAP25B deficiency but is not directly applicable; any treatment evidence belongs in discussion with a neurologist.
Shared loss-of-function claims for SNAP25 and STX1B are contested; the STX1A/VAMP2 one-working-copy explanation is atlas-inferred, unverified and below 0.5 confidence.
Please help check for an existing STX1A group and registry before starting a family network, and consider inviting Konrad Platzer, who works on STX1A and SNAP25, to review the plan.
Let us send one joint inquiry to SLC6A1 Connect asking whether Simons Searchlight could include STX1A-related neurodevelopmental disorder.

Is there a dedicated STX1A patient organization, an enrolling registry or natural history study, an enrolling interventional trial, or a documented animal or cell model with verified access in the atlas?
I’m writing on behalf of families affected by STX1A-related neurodevelopmental disorder.
Our communities share published links to reduced protein function.
Would you join our inquiry about STX1A inclusion in Simons Searchlight?
We would welcome your guidance before taking anything further.
[Your name], on behalf of families affected by STX1A-related neurodevelopmental disorder
